sources.citation: Valdivieso A, Morga B, Degremont L, Mege M, Courtay G, Dorant Y, Escoubas J-M, Gawra J, de Lorgeril J, Mitta G, Cosseau C, Vidal-Dupiol J (2025). DNA methylation landscapes before and after Pacific Oyster Mortality Syndrome are different within and between resistant and susceptible Magallana gigas. Science of the Total Environment 962:178385.
sources.read: full text (HAL accepted manuscript, hal-04901984); supplementary workbook mmc10.xlsx Tables S1-S18 (S4, S5, S7, S9, S11, S13-S18 tallied); supplementary Figs S3 (global methylation) and S4 (PCA) viewed

caveats: The paper compares T1 with T0 within each phenotype; the shared model's time jobs pool both phenotypes (with each oyster as a block), so those verdicts are approximate and at most partly.

claims.statement: Genome-wide CpG methylation is low, about 12-13 % per library (individual values roughly 11.5-13.6 % in Fig. S3 across tissues, phenotypes and times); the paper gives no single number in the text, value read from the figure.
claims.re_derived: 11.31% (mean over 40 samples, all samples; CpG calls pooled per library); paper 12.6%
claims.rule: |difference| <= 2.0 points: replicated; <= 5.0: partly

claims.statement: In gills, global methylation is consistently higher after POMS infection (T1) than before (T0), by about 0.54 percentage points.
claims.re_derived: time T1 11.46% vs T0 11.05% (difference +0.41 points, n = 10 vs 10, permutation p = 0.0065, within tissue_type = G)
claims.rule: same direction and p < 0.05 (or, when group sizes cannot reach 0.05, complete separation): replicated; same direction: partly; opposite: not replicated

claims.statement: In mantle, global methylation is consistently higher at T1 than at T0, by about 0.48 percentage points.
claims.re_derived: time T1 11.54% vs T0 11.20% (difference +0.35 points, n = 10 vs 10, permutation p = 0.001, within tissue_type = M)
claims.rule: same direction and p < 0.05 (or, when group sizes cannot reach 0.05, complete separation): replicated; same direction: partly; opposite: not replicated

claims.statement: Global methylation in gills is higher in susceptible than resistant oysters (one-way ANOVA across the four phenotype x time groups, F = 4.62, P = 0.005); in Fig. S3A the only group differing significantly is susceptible T1 (~13.2 % vs ~12.4-12.8 % for the others).
claims.re_derived: phenotype_class S 11.41% vs R 11.10% (difference +0.32 points, n = 10 vs 10, permutation p = 0.0524, within tissue_type = G)
claims.rule: same direction and p < 0.05 (or, when group sizes cannot reach 0.05, complete separation): replicated; same direction: partly; opposite: not replicated

claims.statement: Global methylation in mantle is higher in susceptible than resistant oysters (one-way ANOVA, F = 7.49, P = 0.002); in Fig. S3B the difference is driven by susceptible T1 (~12.9-13 %), while at T0 susceptible medians are slightly below resistant ones.
claims.re_derived: phenotype_class S 11.43% vs R 11.31% (difference +0.12 points, n = 10 vs 10, permutation p = 0.351, within tissue_type = M)
claims.rule: same direction and p < 0.05 (or, when group sizes cannot reach 0.05, complete separation): replicated; same direction: partly; opposite: not replicated

claims.statement: In PCAs of CpGs common to all samples (1,886,331 in gills, 1,806,224 in mantle), samples cluster mainly by source population (each oyster's T0 and T1 sit together; population 5, SC18, separates on PC1), PC1 and PC2 each explaining about 8-11 % of variance.
claims.re_derived: population explains 97% (adjusted R^2) of PC1 (14.43% of variance), the larger of PC1 and PC2; PCA of job time.G
claims.rule: adjusted R^2 >= 0.5 replicated; >= 0.2 partly

claims.statement: Infection (time) has only a subtle effect on the methylation landscape: T0 and T1 samples do not separate in the PCA, nor do phenotypes.
claims.re_derived: time explains 0% (adjusted R^2) of PC2 (11.87% of variance), the larger of PC1 and PC2; PCA of job time.G
claims.rule: the paper reports no separation: adjusted R^2 < 0.2 replicated; < 0.5 partly

claims.statement: In susceptible gills, T1 vs T0 gave 3069 DMRs located in 2014 genes.
claims.re_derived: job time.G, timeT1: gene_body: 1468 genes at FDR < 0.05 (lambda 1.442); promoter: 24 genes at FDR < 0.05 (lambda 0.737); paper 2014 DMGs
claims.rule: genes vs genes: within 3x of the paper's count replicated; fewer or more but some: partly; none: not replicated; approximate: our job pools over phenotype_class (paper: S only), so at most partly; test statistics are inflated (lambda 1.442 > 1.3), so the count is not trusted: at most partly

claims.statement: Resistant and susceptible oysters already carry distinct methylation patterns before exposure (T0), irrespective of population origin; the paper reports no plain R-vs-S DMR count at T0, only the filtered epibiomarker sets (C24).
claims.re_derived: phenotype_class R vs S within time T0 is a registered contrast, but the paper gives no count or direction for it; only gene-level example is C20

claims.where: Abstract; Results 3.4; Fig. S7; Table S14
claims.statement: 31 immune-related genes carry DMRs after infection in all four tissue x phenotype comparisons (from 222, 185, 181 and 284 immune-related DMR genes in S gills, R gills, S mantle, R mantle), with contrasting directions between phenotypes.
claims.re_derived: intersection of four stratified T1-vs-T0 gene lists filtered by the authors' immune-gene annotation; could be approximated as an overlap of our four per-gene time contrasts, but no kind covers overlap counts and the immune flag is author-curated

claims.statement: 1998 candidate phenotype epibiomarker DMRs (1204 gills, 1030 in gene bodies; 794 mantle, 718 in gene bodies) meet |RT0-ST0| >= 20 %, |RT1-ST0| >= 20 % and |RT0-RT1| <= 5 %.
claims.re_derived: multi-criteria DMR filter on group means, not a single DSS contrast; per-region on paper genome coordinates

claims.statement: 164 gene-body candidate site (POMS exposure) epibiomarkers (66 of 68 DMRs in gills, 98 of 128 in mantle) meet |ST0-RT0| <= 5 %, |ST0-RT1| >= 20 % and |RT0-RT1| >= 20 %; note the abstract's 164 counts gene-body DMRs while its 1998 counts all DMRs.
claims.re_derived: multi-criteria DMR filter on group means; per-region on paper genome coordinates

claims.statement: Genes with DMRs after infection overlap between phenotypes: 527 in gills (277 with the same direction: 157 hyper, 120 hypo) and 788 in mantle (384 same direction: 213 hyper, 171 hypo).
claims.re_derived: overlap between two stratified time contrasts; no kind for gene-list overlap, though it could be approximated from our per-gene results

claims.statement: Genes with DMRs after infection are enriched for immunity, signalling, metabolism and transport GO terms and KEGG pathways (e.g. response to virus and DNA damage response in hypermethylated S-gill genes; mitophagy in hypermethylated R-gill genes).

claims.statement: The cohabitation challenge worked: survival differed among populations (15 % in SC18/#5 to 85 % in Thau/#1, log-rank P <= 0.001), and at T1 OsHV-1 load was higher in susceptible than resistant tissues (Mann-Whitney W = 23, P = 0.032).
